label: Airport
description: A commercial-service airport (14 CFR Part 139 certificate, TSA Airport Security Program under 49 CFR 1542): terminal, airfield, airlines and tenants, TSA/CBP, FIDS/AODB/CUPPS/BHS/PACS and airfield systems. Plans: the Airport Emergency Plan (139.325, with UAS response instructions), the Airport Certification Manual, the ASP and its cybersecurity amendments, and the SMS.

vocabulary.frontline: gate agents, duty managers, ramp supervisors, TSA supervisors, airline station managers

it: CUPPS / CUSS common-use check-in and kiosks
ot: passenger boarding bridges, pre-conditioned air and 400 Hz ground power

roles.name: Director of Operations (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns the terminal, the airfield and the people in them.

roles.name: IT Director (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the systems, the investigation and the restoration.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns the narrative: social media, press, the website.

roles.name: Airport Security Coordinator (Law Enforcement)
roles.description: Owns physical order, the sterile area and the police response.

roles.name: Airline Station Manager (Tenant Liaison)
roles.description: Owns the flights, the passengers at the gates and the airline staff.

roles.name: Emergency Manager (AEP Coordinator)
roles.description: Owns the Airport Emergency Plan, the EOC and the triennial full-scale exercise.

roles.name: ARFF Chief
roles.description: Owns aircraft rescue and firefighting, its index and staffing, and mutual-aid calls.

roles.name: Facilities / Maintenance Director
roles.description: Owns airfield lighting, the BHS, power, HVAC and the fuel farm coordination.

outsideParties: FAA (ATCT, Airports District Office, Part 139 inspector)
airline station managers and corporate operations
system vendors (AODB, CUPPS, BHS, PACS, ALCMS)
a certified state or local counter-UAS law-enforcement team (SAFER SKIES Act authority, in effect since 1 Jul 2026)
mediaChannels: passenger posts on X/Twitter and Instagram

sceneAnchors.public: inside an airport passenger terminal: check-in counters, rows of dark powered-off departure boards, overhead wayfinding signs seen as plain shapes, luggage carts, high ceilings, large windows
sceneAnchors.control: inside an airport operations center: a long console desk with operators in polo shirts, a wall of dark monitors, desk radios, subdued lighting
sceneAnchors.exterior: on an airport apron beside a jet bridge: a parked airliner, baggage tugs and cones, a fuel truck, overcast daylight
sceneAnchors.publicScreensDark: inside a dim airport terminal concourse: crowds waiting at check-in counters, luggage carts, high ceilings, large windows

noiseExamples: vending machines dispensing cans on their own
a password-reset request from a concessionaire
pressureExamples: a passenger tweet with a photo of the wrong gate
a community Facebook rumor about a terror attack
a TV assignment desk going live in 15 minutes
an airline station manager threatening to pull staff
a drone reported off the approach end with the tower holding arrivals and no one sure who may act against it
